text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal began his comeback from 18 months of injury with a remarkable three-under-par 69 in the first round of the Desert Classic on Thursday.

Three birdies in the last four holes of the 7,102-yard Emirates Course lifted the 31-year-old Spaniard into a strong position to achieve his first objective of making the halfway cut after the second round is played on Friday.

Olazabal, the 1994 U.S. Masters champion, has been plagued for 18 months with foot problems that threatened to consign him to a wheelchair for life until a German doctor put him on the road to recovery.
"Obviously I'm pleased but I have to say I wasn't as fully concentrated in the same way as I would have been if what I've been through didn't happen," he said.

Olazabal's 69 left him four shots behind joint first round leaders Colin Montgomerie of Britain, the European number one and defending champion, and unheralded Spaniard Domingo Hospital. They carded 65s, seven under par.
